newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-$1 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-$1 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were steady to mostly $0.50, instances $1.00 lower, pressured by soft packer demand amid plans for light weekend slaughter, dealers said.
Hog slaughter Saturday was pegged at 20,000 to 25,000 head, compared with 25,000 a week ago and 13,000 a year ago, according to analysts' estimates.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $57.00 to $57.50 per cwt in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants.

Indiana hog sales were extremely light at $0.50 to $1.00 lower prices, with $57.00 to $57.50 quoted in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country, with a few to $58.00 at plants.

High heat and humidity was moving into the corn belt Friday and expected to last through the weekend, which could limit marketings, the livestock dealers said. Temperatures were seen in the mid-to-upper 90's degree Fahrenheit, with humidity heat index levels into 100, they said.
